name: Extreme heat
value: Severe heatwave, Cape York Peninsula (17 Nov)
summary: BoM severe heatwave warning for Queensland's Peninsula renewed on 17 Nov; no deadly top-tier event found
state: The Bureau of Meteorology's warning issued at 1:24pm on 17 Nov keeps severe heatwave conditions over the Peninsula district, with maximums in the high 30s to near 40°C, intensifying until mid-week before easing; the North Tropical Coast and Tablelands have dropped to low intensity (WillyWeather, citing BoM). A regional severe warning meets the Watch line. No deadly heatwave under top-tier warnings across a large population was found as of 17 Nov.
for_you: People in far north Queensland should follow Bureau of Meteorology warnings and Queensland Health heat advice. Older people, young children, outdoor workers and those with chronic illness are most exposed.
rubric_hit: Regional BoM severe heatwave warning = Watch; no deadly top-tier event (Alert line)

sources.title: WillyWeather — BoM heatwave warning for Queensland (IDQ21013)

why: Heat is the deadliest weather hazard globally, straining power grids, crops and health systems.
drivers: Heat domes, climate warming, season, humidity, urban heat islands.

rubric.alert: Deadly heatwave with top-tier official warnings across a large population.
rubric.watch: Heatwave warnings across a major region, or national temperature records.
rubric.normal: No major heatwaves affecting large populations.
